---
name: subring-under-letI-action-hides-the-map
description: FixedPoints.subring built under a letI action unfolds membership to that action's smul, so rw on the underlying map "finds no occurrence"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When you define `S := letI := myAction; FixedPoints.subring R G`, membership `x ∈ S`
unfolds to `∀ g, g • x = x` **for the `letI` action's `smul`** — not syntactically to
whatever ring map the action was built from. So `intro g; rw [myMap_apply ...]` fails with
"did not find an occurrence of the pattern" on a goal that visibly contains the pattern.

**Why:** the tactic sees the action's `smul` projection, and the reducibility path back to
the map is not a syntactic match.

**How to apply:** state your own `mem_S : x ∈ S ↔ ∀ g, myMap g x = x := Iff.rfl` next to
the definition, and route every proof through `mem_S.mpr fun g => _` instead of `intro g`.
The `Iff.rfl` proves the two spellings *are* the same; entering through it is what puts the
goal in the spelling your lemmas are stated in.

pin (mathlib has `isUnit_iff_exists`, `IsUnit.of_mul_eq_one` behind `[IsDedekindFiniteMonoid]`,
and `IsUnit.mul_left_inj` for cancellation). A plausible-sounding name is the cheapest thing
to check and the most expensive to guess — see [[absence-claims-need-the-whole-project]].
